en: Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling that is accompanied by a refuge, there arises a state not accompanied by a refuge and not associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling that is accompanied by a refuge, there arises a state not accompanied by a refuge and not associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a state accompanied by a refuge...

Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling that is non-conflict (*araṇa*), there arise states that are neither conflict nor associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and associated with pleasant feeling, there arises a state that is neither conflict nor associated with pleasant feeling, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, there are four; in the case of object condition, two ... pe ... in the case of resultant condition, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, four.

Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling that is not accompanied by clinging (*saraṇa*), there arises a state not accompanied by clinging and not associated with painful feeling through root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of root condition, there are three;
in the case of object condition, two ... pe ... in the case of resultant condition, one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is a refuge, there arises a state not a refuge and not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … [In the case of root condition] there are four;
in the case of object condition (*ārammaṇa*), two … [and so on] … in the case of resultant condition (*vipāka*), one … [and so on] … in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), four.
